key_insight: Accounting for function-preserving parameter symmetries yields covering-number bounds with exponent S−H rather than S and a factorial divisor G from channel permutations.
engineering_relevance: These bounds sharpen capacity estimates and statistical risk guarantees while helping explain weight rebalancing and flat directions in neural-network optimization.
method: Characterize quasianalytic function-preserving parameter maps as positive channel scalings and channel permutations.
Quotient out these symmetries across fully connected, convolutional, and residual ReLU/Leaky ReLU networks.
Prove covering-number upper and lower bounds and extend the analysis to general continuous piecewise-linear activations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical proofs rather than empirical benchmarks: matching lower bounds establish exponent sharpness, with the permutation divisor attained for one-hidden-layer and generically identifiable networks.
watch_item: The full permutation-factor improvement is established under specific architecture or identifiability conditions, so its tightness should not be assumed for every network.
paper_title: Sharp Covering-Number Bounds for Feedforward ReLU Networks via Parameter Symmetries
